flags.note: The construction כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא + imperfect verb mirrors Greek ἵνα μή + subjunctive for negative purpose. Native Hebrew would use פֶּן or לְבִלְתִּי.
The שֶׁ relative clause 'who judges her' after עָצוּם האדון יהוה creates an awkward construction. Native Hebrew would more likely use a participle הַשֹּׁפֵט אוֹתָהּ or restructure entirely.
The construction בְּאִם שֶׁ + imperfect mirrors Greek ὅταν + subjunctive for temporal clauses. Native Hebrew would use בִּרְאוֹתָם or כַּאֲשֶׁר יִרְאוּ.
The בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא construction for negative causation reflects Greek διότι οὐ pattern. Native Hebrew would prefer כִּי אֵין קֹנֶה or similar.
The שֶׁל genitive construction 'vessels of silver' shows Aramaic/later Hebrew influence. Classical Hebrew would use construct state כְּלֵי כֶסֶף.
The relative clause structure with הָיָה + prepositional phrase is awkward. Native Hebrew would more naturally use a construct relationship or participial phrase.
The word order with the demonstrative אֵילוּ הַדְּבָרִים after the relative clause is unnatural. Hebrew would place the object closer to the verb.
The temporal construction בְּשָׁעַת שֶׁ + perfect reflects Greek influence. Native Hebrew would use בִּרְאוֹתָם or כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאוּ.
The relative clause with הָיָה + לְ expressing possession mirrors Greek constructions. Hebrew would more naturally use בַּעֲלֵי הַסְּפִינוֹת or אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם סְפִינוֹת.
